title: [D5 Tools] Replay mode — read stored responses, never re-query
summary: `helena.tools.ProviderTool` now takes a required `replay` keyword: a replay resolves every lookup from the stored response for its source, endpoint and indicator, serves an expired record explicitly `stale` rather than re-querying it, and turns a missing stored response into a new typed refusal `no_stored_response` instead of a live call. `helena.network.no_network()` is the hard guard — `lookup` arms it around the whole dispatch whenever the tool is a replay, so any new outbound connection raises `NetworkAttempted` where it was attempted. The retrieval trace already recorded cache-hit versus live-query and the underlying record's retrieval time (task 35/36); this increment extends those tests to the replay pair and adds the zero-outbound-request test at both the tool boundary and through a whole analyst run.
assumption_validated: That a replay can be a mode of the SAME dispatch rather than a second lookup path, and that the property can be demonstrated rather than argued. Both held. A replayed answer is assembled by the code that assembled the recorded one — measured byte-for-byte: same evidence rows, same `response_version`, same native body, same `retrieved_at` — and the adapter (the only thing in the layer that can reach a provider, since `helena.tools` imports no HTTP machinery) is never called. A negative result worth recording: a process-wide socket guard cannot be armed for the whole of a replayed AGENT run, because hosted inference is also a network call; the guard therefore scopes to one lookup, and the claim it supports is 'nothing new leaves the process while a replay lookup runs', not 'a replayed run makes no network calls at all'.
makes_buildable: Task 42 (orchestration) and task 43 (assessment persistence) get the provider half of `concept/03`'s 'replays from stored results' already built and already guarded: an orchestration replay constructs its tools with `replay=True` (or `providers.threatfox_tool(..., replay=True)`) and needs the store, not the credential — the adapter is never called, so the key is never revealed. Everything a replayed lookup produces is already in the shapes those tasks store: `RetrievalStep.outcome` is `cache_hit`, `RetrievalStep.retrieved_at` is the underlying record's time, `RunBudget.cost()` carries `live_queries=0` / `cache_hits=n`, and the disclosure ledger is empty. The one thing still missing for a full assessment replay is the stored assessment itself, which is task 43. `helena.network.no_network()` is reusable by anything that needs to assert an offline section.

verification.detail: 1577 passed, 2 skipped in 567.95s (0:09:27). Full suite, against the real migrated engine. New: tests/test_replay.py (8) for the guard — including a real query against the real engine connection inside it — plus 11 replay tests in tests/test_tools.py and 2 whole-run replay tests in tests/test_analyst.py. The two skips are pre-existing conditional live-model skips (tests/test_agents.py:1018 schema_invalid, tests/test_analyst.py:1724 timed_out), not new.

invariant_conflicts.step: Make a missing stored response a typed failure in replay rather than a live call
invariant_conflicts.invariant: concept/instruction.md §2 — `stale`/`failed`/`missing`/`no_match`/a typed error are five things and never collapse; §3 — a contract field or vocabulary is not a session's to widen
invariant_conflicts.resolution: Implemented as a typed REFUSAL (`helena.tools.NO_STORED_RESPONSE = "no_stored_response"`), not as a `QueryFailure`. Two reasons, and the second is decisive. Nothing was queried, so there is no provider to attribute an outage to — the argument the other four refusals rest on, and calling it a `transport_error` would record an outage that did not happen. And a replay miss could not have been a retrieval step at all: `helena.contracts.v1.RETRIEVAL_OUTCOMES` is `(cache_hit, live_query)`, a miss is neither, and widening a frozen contract to record the absence of a row is an escalation this increment did not need. It is agent-visible, typed and countable (logged as `tools.lookup.refused` with its reason), and it stays distinct from `no_match` — the provider saying it lists nothing — which is nobody having asked. ADR-0031 §2.

deferred: Replaying a whole ASSESSMENT. What is here is a replayed provider lookup. A replayed agent run still calls the model (a different quota, a different disclosure channel), and the stored assessment a full replay would be reconstructed from is not written by any increment yet — `concept/03-architecture.md` puts that in Orchestration, and it is task 42/43.

Pruning the store. Nothing is evicted and nothing bounds the growth, so how far back a replay can reach is bounded only by disk. `concept/08` still lists the retention horizon as open; ADR-0025 and ADR-0031 §6 both say so.

A `--replay` surface of any kind (CLI flag, config key). `replay` is the caller's statement about one run, passed at construction; a deployment does not have a replay setting, and a config key with one value is what `concept/instruction.md` §1 refuses.
lessons: REPLAY MODE CANNOT BE ARMED FOR A WHOLE AGENT RUN, AND THE REASON IS THE MODEL. A process-wide socket guard held open across an analyst run would block hosted inference, which is also a network call. So `helena.network.no_network()` is armed by `ProviderTool.lookup` around ONE dispatch and released after it, and the claim it supports is bounded accordingly: nothing new leaves the process while a replay lookup runs. Anything later that wants a whole-run offline assertion has to exempt the model endpoint deliberately, not by accident.

THE GUARD BLOCKS `connect`, NOT WRITES, AND THAT BOUND IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN LAZY. A replay reads its stored responses out of the streaming engine over a psycopg connection opened before the guard is armed; blocking sends on an already-open socket would make the guard airtight and make replay impossible. `tests/test_replay.py::test_an_already_open_connection_to_the_store_keeps_working_inside_the_guard` executes a real query against the real engine inside the guard, so the bound is pinned by a test rather than left in a docstring. What that means for a later adapter: one holding a pooled connection open across a live phase and a replay phase would slip through. `helena.providers` opens a socket per call, so none does today.

`helena.tools` MAY NOT IMPORT `socket`, AND THAT IS WHY THE GUARD IS ITS OWN MODULE. `tests/test_tools.py` reads `tools.py`'s AST and fails on `urllib`/`http`/`socket`/`ssl` (task 34), which is what makes 'the agent sees a tool, never an HTTP client and never a key' a property of the code. `helena.providers` is the obvious home and cannot be one — it imports `helena.tools`. `helena/network.py` holds one context manager, one exception, no URL and no client, and is registered in `tests/test_package_layout.py`'s SUPPORT_MODULES with that reasoning. It is NOT named `replay`, because `concept/03` puts 'replays from stored results' in Orchestration and that runner does not exist.

AN EXPIRED RECORD IS SERVED IN A REPLAY AND CARRIES NO FAILURE STEP. Nothing is ever evicted, so the record is still citable and `concept/02`'s `stale` is exactly what it is. The live path's stale fallback carries a `QueryFailure` beside it because a provider was reached and did not answer; a replay reached nothing, and reporting a timeout nobody experienced would be inventing an outage to explain an age. Found while writing it: `_served` derived its LOG LINE's status from whether a failure was passed — correct for both live callers, wrong the first time a replay served an expired record with no outage. It now derives it from the same expiry the evidence rows are dated against.

A REPLAY NEEDS THE STORE AND NOT THE CREDENTIAL. The adapter is the only thing the `Secret` is ever handed to, and no branch of a replay reaches it, so a replayed run never reveals the key. That is a property worth keeping when the orchestration replay runner is built: it can run where the provider key is absent.
failed_approaches: Putting `replay` on `RunScope` was considered and rejected before it was written. It is the right SCOPE — one run, taken from the request, not the model's to choose — and the wrong object: `RunScope` is the tenant and the sensor and its whole argument is about isolation, and `RunScope.of(request)` would have needed a default because `AgentRequest` has no replay field (adding one is a contract change). A constructor keyword on the tool says the same thing without touching either.

Defaulting `replay` to `False` on `ProviderTool` was considered and rejected. Forgetting to pass `replay=True` when replaying is the exact failure the task exists to prevent, and a default is what lets it be forgotten. The cost is four construction sites, all in this repository; the test builders in `tests/test_tools.py` and `tests/test_analyst.py` keep a `replay=False` default of their own so that only the replay tests mention it.

Making the replay miss a `QueryFailure` with a new reason was considered and rejected — see invariant_conflicts. `QUERY_FAILURE_REASONS` are provider outages, and `RETRIEVAL_OUTCOMES` has no value a replay miss could be recorded under without widening a frozen contract.

Arming the guard once around a whole analyst run, and requiring `lookup` to assert it was armed, was designed and dropped: the model call is a network call, so the guard would have broken every replayed run at the first inference request. See the first lesson.
next_session_should_know: Task 42 is orchestration and task 43 is persistence; this task built the provider half of replay. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE MODE IS ONE REQUIRED KEYWORD AND IT HAS NO DEFAULT: `tools.ProviderTool(..., replay=True|False)` and `providers.threatfox_tool(..., replay=...)`. `tool.replay` reads it back. There is no config key, no CLI flag and no request field — it is the caller's statement about one run, and a mode a caller could vary per lookup is one a tool loop could vary per turn. (2) A REPLAY MISS IS `tools.NO_STORED_RESPONSE`, A REFUSAL, AND IT IS A FIFTH KIND OF ABSENCE. Not `no_match` (the provider listed nothing), not a `QueryFailure` (nothing was queried), and it could not have been a `RetrievalStep` — `RETRIEVAL_OUTCOMES` is `(cache_hit, live_query)`. If a later increment wants the absence on the assessment, it arrives as a refusal in `Analysis.retrievals`, not as a trace step, and turning it into a `Gap` is a decision somebody should make deliberately rather than discover. (3) AN EXPIRED RECORD IS SERVED IN A REPLAY, EXPLICITLY `stale`, WITH NO FAILURE STEP. Refusing anything past its retention would make a replay of a three-week-old assessment return nothing, which is the opposite of what replay is for. (4) THE GUARD IS `helena.network.no_network()` AND ITS BOUND IS EXACT: it refuses `socket.socket.connect`, `connect_ex` and `socket.getaddrinfo` — every NEW outbound connection — and deliberately does NOT block traffic on an already-open one, because the store is read over a psycopg connection opened before it is armed. A `NetworkAttempted` propagates; it is never a typed result. DO NOT try to arm it around a whole agent run: hosted inference is a network call and it would block the model. (5) A REPLAY NEEDS THE STORE AND NOT THE KEY. The credential only ever reaches the adapter and no replay branch reaches the adapter. (6) THE MEASUREMENT OF 'IT DID NOT RE-QUERY' IS THE ADAPTER, NOT A COUNTER — task 35's rule, reused. Both replay test suites build the replaying tool with an adapter that RAISES on contact, so there is no path in which a provider was reached and the assertions still hold. (7) WHAT IS NOT REPLAYABLE YET IS AN ASSESSMENT. A replayed run still calls the model, and no assessment is stored. `concept/03`'s Orchestration row — 'replays from stored results' — is task 42/43's, and `docs/decisions/0031-replay-at-the-tool-boundary.md` §6 says exactly what this increment does and does not make replayable.
